introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

The paper contains eight questions.
enonce_intro_markdown: A uniform rod $AB$ of mass $3m$ and length $4a$ has a particle of mass $2m$ attached to the end $B$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the moment of inertia of the system about an axis through $A$ which is perpendicular to the plane of the rod is $48ma^2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Moment of inertia of a uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $\ell$ about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod: $\tfrac13M\ell^2$.

Rod: $\tfrac13(3m)(4a)^2 = \tfrac13(3m)(16a^2) = 16ma^2$.

Particle at $B$ (distance $4a$ from $A$): $(2m)(4a)^2 = 32ma^2$.

$$I_A = 16ma^2 + 32ma^2 = 48ma^2.$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the distance, from $A$, of the centroid of the system. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take moments about $A$. The centre of mass of the rod is at distance $2a$ from $A$, and the particle is at distance $4a$:

$$\bar{x}\,(3m+2m) = 3m(2a) + 2m(4a) = 14ma$$

$$\bar{x} = \frac{14ma}{5m} = \frac{14a}{5} = 2.8a.$$

The centroid is at a distance $\dfrac{14a}{5}$ from $A$, on the rod.
themes: centre of mass of composite bodies

questions.enonce_markdown: The rod is smoothly hinged at a horizontal axis through $A$ and then released from rest. Show that when the rod makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal, $12a\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)^2 = 7g\sin\theta$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The hinge is smooth, so mechanical energy is conserved. The rod starts at rest in the horizontal position and turns downwards through the angle $\theta$.

**Loss of potential energy.** The centre of mass of the system (mass $5m$, at distance $\tfrac{14a}{5}$ from $A$) falls a vertical distance $\tfrac{14a}{5}\sin\theta$:

$$\Delta\mathrm{PE} = 5mg\cdot\frac{14a}{5}\sin\theta = 14mga\sin\theta.$$

**Gain of kinetic energy.** The system rotates about the fixed axis through $A$ with angular speed $\dot\theta$ (starting from rest):

$$\mathrm{KE} = \tfrac12 I_A\dot\theta^2 = \tfrac12(48ma^2)\dot\theta^2 = 24ma^2\dot\theta^2.$$

**Energy equation.**

$$24ma^2\dot\theta^2 = 14mga\sin\theta \ \Longrightarrow\ 12a\,\dot\theta^2 = 7g\sin\theta,$$

that is $12a\left(\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}\right)^2 = 7g\sin\theta$.
